topic:
When does plan turnover still permit a finite nonparametric upper bound on switching costs? A sharp iid frontier for short health-choice panels. Observe n independent consumers in one known design cell: (Y0,Y1,Y2), fixed initial choice Y0=h0, two observed nonempty menus M1,M2 contained in a universe D={1,...,J}, J finite, and known finite rational prices p_td for d in Mt. Initial h0 belongs to D and may be absent from M1. Utility is -p_td + κ 1{d=Y(t-1)} + λ_d + ε_td, κ≥0 common. Conditional on λ, ε1 and ε2 are iid, have an absolutely continuous distribution on R^J with arbitrary within-period dependence; the mixing law of λ and the conditional shock law are unrestricted. Choices maximize utility, uniquely almost surely. Let P=(P_ab:a∈M1,b∈M2) be the observed path table; assume at least one κ/model rationalizes P. Θ(P) contains every κ≥0 with an exact rationalization; U(P)=sup Θ(P), taking value +∞ if unbounded. Multiple observed cells with arbitrary cell-specific heterogeneity can subsequently be intersected; that is not needed in the kernel.

Precise answer-open theorem problem. For every finite rational design above, construct from its utility-comparison graph a finite price threshold K and an explicit compact terminal path-probability body C∞ such that the exact compatible body Cκ equals C∞ for all κ>K, and prove sharpness in both directions by constructing iid random-utility rationalizations. Derive an observable necessary-and-sufficient criterion for U(P)<∞, expressed using this constructed body rather than a quantifier over structural distributions, and recover the exact U(P) by a finite price-breakpoint search with certified feasibility. Mandatory non-generic core: for J=3, h0∈M1, and every pure-entry or pure-exit menu pair {a,b}↔{a,b,c}, derive a complete explicit analytic characterization of C∞ (a finite Boolean combination of inequalities in the six entries P_ab, with no latent variables, optimization, or unevaluated quantifier elimination), including boundary cases and constructive attainability. Do not presume that corrected Jensen inequalities are complete. Extend computation to any finite J via a certified inner/outer approximation with a proved deterministic error bound. Pair with a confidence set for Θ(P) that covers the entire set with probability at least 1-α uniformly over the stated model and preserves +∞ when the terminal body cannot be rejected. Exact formulas/inequality lists are the theorem’s output, not assumed hypotheses.

Computation and inference: At fixed κ, enumerate deterministic response tables f: one first-period choice and a second-period choice for each a∈M1. Retain f iff one shock vector z satisfies all strict utility inequalities simultaneously; solve this difference-constraint feasibility problem with cycle tests. For probabilities q on retained tables define v_ab(q)=(sum_f q_f 1{f1=a})(sum_g q_g 1{g2(a)=b}). The known iid mixture gives Cκ=conv{v(q):q in simplex}; prove attainability with continuous shocks inside open patches. At T=2 this is a linear image of normalized completely-positive matrices E[qq′]. That observation is only a computation starting point. Enumerate price breakpoints where response-table feasibility changes; terminal graph is after the last breakpoint. A rational simplex grid plus convex hull LP gives inner approximations; the quadratic map’s Lipschitz bound gives a certified outer inflation, with refinement until a requested positive precision is reached. The J=3 analytic elimination and sharpness are mandatory; a black-box copositive/QE call alone fails the contract. Estimate all m=|M1||M2| path probabilities by multinomial frequencies. Invert certified distance-to-Cκ tests using a simultaneous multinomial concentration region, including optimization error. For example a sup-norm Hoeffding box radius sqrt(log(2m/α)/(2n)) supplies a finite-sample starting point; certify uniform whole-set coverage and consistent finite-upper-bound declaration whenever D∞(P)>0. No uniform consistency at D∞=0 is claimed. This rung is supporting, not the novelty: Tamer–Walker 2608.25814 already studies general PMF-to-identified-set Bayesian inference.

Grounding and exclusions: Theorem 2.3(a) proves P(Y1∈A,Y2∈A)≥P(Y1∈A)^2 under structural-utility dominance and a common menu. Its load-bearing samplewise containment fails with entrants; conditioning on selecting continuing plans does not restore the latent mixture. Appendix proof, pp.50–52, makes this failure explicit. The supplied paper pp.20–21 excludes changing menus and loses year-pairs crossing 2011; p.40 leaves the nonparametric varying-menu problem open. Closest: Mbakop (2023), arXiv:2305.15691, https://arxiv.org/html/2305.15691v1 — Prop.2.14 gives nonpolyhedral iid bodies; Example3.5/Thm3.6 compute sharp stationarity inequalities; Remark3.9 and footnote50 show the health assumption is iid-equivalent, already represent its CCPs as mixtures of products, and show his inequalities complement the Pakes inequalities. Difference: an explicit complete turnover upper-tail frontier and analytic three-plan iid body, not generic sharp-set computation. Generic PMF/set Bayesian inference is closed-by:Tamer–Walker 2608.25814 (Aug2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25814. Live exact-pair and citing searches on Sept7,2026 found no result resolving this turnover/conditional-iid frontier; absence from bounded searches is not proof of novelty. Author research pages and NBER still point to June/July2025 paper; SSRN metadata reports Apr23,2026 revision, and a second author-hosted PDF returned HTTP403, so a full independent later-revision comparison remains a presolve check. Internal collision_snapshot.json was checked only for dedup: no health, menu, Pakes, Mbakop, multinomial, or relevant switching-cost title; no failed/downgraded run contents were read.

Consumer: Pakes et al.’s published NBER working paper 29025, health-plan application §§3,5: it drops observations experiencing plan entry/exit, and cannot use year-pairs crossing 2011 because too few menus remain stable. The result permits using those observed menu-change comparisons while retaining flexible fixed effects and iid nonparametric disturbances, and states exactly when a finite switching-cost ceiling survives. A journal-published additional consumer is Polyakova (2016), AEJ:Applied 8(3),165–195, Regulation of Insurance with Adverse Selection and Switching Costs: Evidence from Medicare Part D, DOI 10.1257/app.20150004: structural estimates of inertia feed risk-sorting and regulation counterfactuals. It could use the resulting nonparametric ceiling as a robustness restriction on switching-cost magnitudes in stable-quality menu-turnover cells; the theorem does not itself identify welfare or validate cells with changed plan quality.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived strict-cycle feasibility, continuous-shock convexification, finite rational price-breakpoint saturation, and the equivalence between a finite switching-cost ceiling and positive distance from the terminal probability body. It obtained an explicit analytic entry body for one relative-price sign and two informative boundary faces. A legal all-positive entry table has an exact upper endpoint of four, passes the corrected Jensen inequality, and admits a terminal exchangeability rationalization while violating the iid terminal restriction. Exact rational reconstruction, terminal separating inequalities, strict patch margins, and numerical analytic-body checks were reproduced. Checks included all nine terminal response classes, zero probabilities, unattained endpoints, initial-plan exit, and singleton menus. Current primary comparisons found no affirmative collision; the April 2026 SSRN revision remains inaccessible and requires retrieval and comparison.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the constructive latent-free analytic projection for negative entry with both off-diagonal probabilities positive, zero-sign entry, and all six exit classes, including every boundary case and attaining mixture.
EARLY KILL TEST: Derive the negative-entry allocation formula and compare its support values with exact quadratic optimization over all twenty response-pair curves. A discrepancy kills that formula; inability to complete the analytic elimination requires reassessing the field-tier scope.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The common-menu samplewise-containment argument of Pakes et al. fails when an entrant or unavailable incumbent changes the compared choice set, and conditioning on a continuing-plan choice changes the latent mixing distribution. Mbakop's results show that direct iid response-probability enumeration does not restore polyhedrality. The response-table reduction instead produces a nonnegative quadratic image whose latent variables must be eliminated without losing factorization, zero-cell faces, or continuous-shock attainability. The unresolved proof boundary is the complete projection for negative- and zero-sign entry regimes and all exit classes, including singular boundary points where ordinary Jacobian-rank arguments fail.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite price threshold and explicit compact terminal body, a necessary-and-sufficient observable criterion for a finite upper endpoint, an exact finite-breakpoint endpoint formula, and a finite Boolean inequality characterization of every three-plan entry and exit body with constructive iid rationalizations.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation connects persistent plan choices, fixed-effect confounding, switching-cost upper bounds, and the empirical loss caused by the common-menu restriction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Plan persistence mixes state dependence with stable person-by-plan tastes -> iid restrictions can bound switching costs while retaining flexible fixed effects -> entry and exit remove the comparisons used by existing bounds -> characterize exactly when turnover still permits a finite ceiling

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate deterministic response patches, derive support functions of conditional-iid probability bodies, and prove sharpness using continuous shocks supported inside utility-order regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The terminal turnover body is the same mixture-of-products object, specialized to a small geometry where explicit nonlinear projection may be possible.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile finite response functions and observational restrictions into polynomial programs and reconstruct structural witnesses from feasible latent weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the raw polynomial representation that must be analytically eliminated while retaining exact witness reconstruction.

method_exemplars.technique: Project empirical choice frequencies onto a random-utility cone and bootstrap a test of probability-body membership with binding restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Switching-cost-set inference likewise inverts membership tests, although the conditional-iid terminal body is curved rather than polyhedral.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether finite upper-tail saturation and an observable finite-switching-cost criterion persist for three or more post-initial choices with repeated menu entry and exit under conditionally iid shocks.

open_problems.why_unsolved: For two observed choices, iid mixing can be encoded through second moments of latent response probabilities. With longer histories, the same latent type generates higher-order products while lagged choices alter the feasible response map at every history. Pairwise restrictions do not characterize the resulting completely-positive tensor cone, and support reductions for ordinary mixtures need not preserve every history-contingent coordinate. The first proof step that changes is therefore the two-copy convexification: it must become a history-consistent higher-order moment representation with a finite support theorem and a continuous-shock realization for every factor.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A recursive finite-dimensional moment-body characterization for each fixed panel length, with a proof or counterexample for finite price-breakpoint saturation, a necessary-and-sufficient finite-ceiling criterion, a latent-support bound, and a smallest explicit T=3 example.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames longer panels as additional identifying information for separating state dependence from fixed heterogeneity under weak distributional restrictions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Persistence can reflect state dependence or fixed heterogeneity -> short panels yield set identification -> additional histories may tighten or collapse the set -> determine what repeated menu turnover adds or destroys under iid shocks

method_exemplars.technique: Construct history-specific deterministic response types and use support-function arguments to characterize observable bodies under serial restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The longer-panel iid body has the same response-type foundation but replaces the quadratic image by history-consistent higher-order products.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode dynamic potential-outcome restrictions and sharp identified sets as finite programs over latent histories.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its history-enumeration proof clarifies which cross-history consistency constraints must be preserved, although iid products add nonlinearity.

method_exemplars.technique: Push uncertainty in a finite path PMF through a set-valued identification map and prove consistency of the resulting identified-set posterior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A fixed-length extension still maps a finite multinomial path law into a structural set, but through a higher-order nonlinear feasibility map.

open_problems.open_problem: Quantify exactly which finite switching-cost ceilings under menu turnover are created by conditional independence rather than surviving under conditional exchangeability or stationarity of utility shocks.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A finite upper bound may be generated by the product restriction implied by iid shocks rather than by time homogeneity alone. Weakening iid changes the geometry from a curved mixture-of-products body to stationarity or exchangeability response bodies, and the existing inequality families are not nested in a way that makes a Jensen comparison decisive. The first proof step that fails is factorization of conditional path probabilities. Existing searches locate sharp stationarity results and iid nonpolyhedrality separately but no menu-turnover classification of when the endpoint changes from finite to infinite across serial-assumption classes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A design-indexed comparison of the sharp iid, exchangeable, and stationary terminal bodies, including necessary-and-sufficient conditions for equality of their upper endpoints and explicit observable regions where only iid yields a finite ceiling.

writing_exemplar.why: Its organization explicitly compares identification under stationarity, exchangeability, and independence and emphasizes the geometric change caused by iid.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak serial restrictions yield computable response bodies -> iid adds factorization and nonpolyhedral geometry -> existing inequality families are complementary -> isolate which finite switching-cost ceilings genuinely come from independence

method_exemplars.technique: Compute support functions under stationarity, exchangeability, and conditional independence, then compare exposed faces and rationalizing response patches.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is precisely a comparison of these bodies at the switching-cost upper tail under changing menus.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite-program characterizations of stationarity-based sharp sets and invert sample restrictions to obtain confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an operational benchmark for the weaker serial-assumption body against which the nonlinear iid body can be compared.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a sharp sensitivity frontier for the switching-cost upper bound when menu turnover or network changes permit bounded time variation in person-by-plan utility components rather than exact stability.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Health-plan entry and exit frequently coincide with changes in provider networks or contract quality, so the same event that creates turnover can invalidate the stable fixed-effect restriction. Existing practice either discards the affected paths or imposes a parametric utility model. Bounded drift changes response-table feasibility because cross-period comparisons retain unknown alternative-specific drift terms, while iid convexification alone cannot eliminate them. Generic breakdown-frontier machinery does not supply the sharp link between an admissible drift radius and finiteness of the switching-cost ceiling.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified endpoint U(P,delta) under a stated norm bound delta on person-by-plan utility drift, together with the observable breakdown value at which the endpoint becomes infinite and constructive rationalizations on both sides.

writing_exemplar.why: Its provider-network example explains concretely why turnover observations are removed and motivates a bounded-drift analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Flexible fixed effects protect against persistent taste heterogeneity -> identification still requires stable plan-specific tastes -> turnover often accompanies network or quality changes -> quantify how much instability a finite switching-cost conclusion can tolerate

method_exemplars.technique: Index departures from a baseline assumption by an interpretable parameter, derive the boundary where a target conclusion fails, and construct uniform inference for that boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The utility-drift radius plays the role of an assumption-relaxation parameter, while the conclusion is finiteness of the switching-cost endpoint.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate latent dynamic types and prove sharpness under combinations of cross-period restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Bounded plan-value drift can be encoded as restrictions on latent cross-period utility types before imposing iid product structure.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a proof-producing, singularity-robust certifier for the terminal iid body at arbitrary finite J that returns nested inner and outer approximations, exact included-point rationalizations, and checkable excluded-point separators.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A rational simplex grid with Lipschitz inflation gives convergent approximation, but a reusable certifier must also classify boxes touching zero response weights, strict-utility patch boundaries, and lower-dimensional quadratic-image faces. Interval-Newton inclusion can fail at rank-deficient preimages, while generic quantifier elimination does not automatically decode a continuous-shock iid witness or a compact separating certificate. The first source-method step that changes is box classification: it must certify a nonnegative quadratic factor and a strict response-table feasibility margin rather than only a nonsingular polynomial root.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every rational design and epsilon greater than zero, a terminating algorithm returning C_in contained in C_infinity contained in C_out with Hausdorff error at most epsilon, replayable iid witnesses and separators, and explicit runtime and bit-size bounds.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Intersecting cellwise sets is formally simple, but a useful identification result requires design-level conditions ensuring that every false switching-cost value is excluded despite unrestricted heterogeneity within each cell. Each conditional-iid cell contributes a curved, breakpoint-dependent compatibility body, so rank conditions from linear moment-inequality models do not transfer. The missing step is a finite certificate that the intersection of all cellwise compatibility regions is a singleton, including designs where individual cells have infinite upper tails.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient finite certificate in observed cell PMFs and price-menu breakpoints for the intersection of cellwise sharp sets to be a singleton, with an algorithm returning the identified value or a non-singleton certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates pooling narrowly defined cells while retaining rich within-cell heterogeneity and identifies point identification as unfinished work.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rich fixed effects force cellwise partial identification -> heterogeneous prices and menus generate complementary restrictions -> applications already combine many cells -> determine when their intersection identifies one common switching cost

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze when design-specific sharp sets collapse to a point under finite-support covariate variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest short-panel precedent for point identification from multiple discrete designs, although the turnover iid bodies are nonlinear.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cellwise support functions and parameter-region partitions to certify compatibility of a common parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate must combine exactly these probability-body restrictions across menu and price designs.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate bootstrap relaxations of moment constraints while repeatedly solving feasibility problems to obtain uniformly valid projection intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Certified multi-cell feasibility constraints can be inverted using calibrated projection on the common switching-cost coordinate.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conservative finite-sample inversion can preserve the value positive infinity but does not determine how quickly finite-ceiling declarations become possible when the distance to the terminal body tends to zero. Smooth exposed faces may yield Gaussian directional limits, whereas corners, multiple closest points, and quadratic-image self-contact alter both the tangent cone and separation rate. Prior compatibility-frontier work shows that scalar face derivatives can fail to be selector-complete at ties, so the missing first step is an exact tangent and normal-cone characterization of the terminal body.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A stratified theorem giving the minimax separation rate and limiting experiment for finite-versus-infinite endpoint testing at each terminal-body face type, plus a uniformly valid rate-attaining procedure and an impossibility result on the zero-distance boundary where appropriate.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats sampling uncertainty at a robustness frontier as part of the substantive conclusion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conclusions depend on a sensitivity or boundary parameter -> the weakest value overturning the conclusion defines a frontier -> uncertainty becomes nonregular near kinks -> finite switching-cost ceilings need a local theory at terminal-body contact

method_exemplars.technique: Derive limits through Hadamard directional derivatives and use estimated-derivative resampling when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Distance to a body with changing closest faces is directionally but generally not fully differentiable.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent identified sets as criterion contours, derive Hausdorff rates, and calibrate confidence regions from local criterion behavior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Terminal compatibility is a zero-distance criterion whose local contour geometry determines finite-ceiling detectability.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct simultaneous nonasymptotic confidence regions for the full multinomial parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the finite-sample whole-set baseline against which local asymptotic sharpness can be assessed.

literature_map:
Pakes, Porter, Shepard, and Calder-Wang (accessible June 2025 revision, NBER 29025) provide the central health-plan fixed-effect/state-dependence framework and explicitly leave changing-choice-set nonparametrics, sharp computation, and point identification unfinished.
Their application removes consumers facing different plan offerings and cannot use year-pairs crossing the 2011 availability change; only the parametric analysis restores those observations.
Their Theorem 2.3/Jensen construction is a valid outer restriction under a common menu, but Mbakop (2023, arXiv:2305.15691) proves the Pakes inequalities are not sharp and supplies complementary stationarity inequalities.
Mbakop's Proposition 2.14 is the key geometric warning: conditional-iid observable bodies are convex and closed but nonpolyhedral, so a finite linear-inequality catalogue is generally unavailable.
Mbakop's response-patch and support-function machinery is nevertheless the closest identification method for a small analytic turnover body; his iid proof states that extension beyond the binary two-period illustration requires more work.
Khan, Ponomareva, and Tamer (2023, Journal of Econometrics) sharply characterize dynamic binary panels under conditional stationarity and show point identification can occur in short panels, but do not cover multinomial changing menus under conditional iid shocks.
Pakes and Porter (2024, Quantitative Economics) allow arbitrary serial correlation with person-by-product fixed effects but omit state dependence, exposing the tension between flexible serial dependence and switching-cost identification.
Shi, Shum, and Song (2018, Econometrica; arXiv:1604.06145) use cyclic monotonicity for semiparametric panel multinomial choice, an adjacent common-parameter method that does not resolve the iid turnover body.
Torgovitsky (2019, Econometrica) gives sharp program-based dynamic-potential-outcome sets and is a useful history-enumeration analogue for longer panels or bounded taste drift.
Kitamura and Stoye (2018, Econometrica; arXiv:1606.04819) provide testing and bootstrap machinery for random-utility cone membership, the closest frequentist inference analogue once a turnover body is available.
Tamer and Walker (2026, arXiv:2608.25814) address generic PMF-to-identified-set Bayesian inference but do not derive the model-specific terminal body or finite-versus-infinite switching-cost frontier.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) give uniformly valid calibrated projection inference and repeated feasibility algorithms relevant to multi-cell common-parameter inference.
Polyakova (2016, AEJ: Applied) shows that switching-cost magnitudes materially affect Medicare Part D risk sorting and regulation counterfactuals; Handel (2013) and Heiss et al. reinforce the substantive importance of health-plan inertia.
Masten and Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1705.04765) provide the natural sensitivity-frontier template for bounded time variation in person-by-plan tastes when turnover coincides with quality changes.
SSRN metadata reports a Pakes et al. revision dated April 23, 2026, while current author pages still expose the June 2025 PDF; the SSRN delivery returned HTTP 403, so the later revision could not be independently compared.
